Make It All Zeros

AlgorithmsPlace Value

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Clear the table — every number must become zero.
How to play: Press ×2 beside a row to double it, or −1 above/below a column to subtract (Speed up subtracts down to a column minimum of 1). Take back undoes.
Look for the math

Engel asks you to prove that every table of positive integers can be cleared with these two moves. Doubling looks like it makes things worse — yet it is essential.

Why doubling helps

Subtracting from a column decreases every entry there by the same amount. If one cell in the column is already smaller than another, you cannot clear both by subtracts alone. Doubling a row scales that row’s contribution so the column differences can line up. In the language of binary place value, row doubles correspond to shifting bits; column subtracts peel off units.

Always possible

The theorem (Engel, Problem-Solving Strategies) says a finite sequence always exists. The applet’s Speed up only compresses many identical column subtracts into one click when the column’s minimum is greater than 1. Numbers may go negative if you overshoot — the win is still exactly the all-zero table. Tiny boards in the logic test clear by hand; the general proof is the page’s claim.

Try a 1×2 table with Speed up off. Clear it, then turn Speed up on for a taller column and watch several −1s become one click.
